extracted.intended_audience: general readers of Montaigne; educated readers interested in moral/philosophical essays on marriage, love, and social conduct
extracted.subtask_description: A personal/philosophical essay (Montaigne) exploring marriage, love, chastity, sexual behaviour, and social norms; it offers moral judgments, practical counsel, and cultural observations rather than a formal checklist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Observe the laws of marriage and manage liberty prudently
rubrics_metrics.description: “A man must prudently manage his liberty; but having once submitted to obligation, he must confine himself within the laws of common duty.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Once one enters the marital contract, one should accept its ordinary duties and restrain personal liberty accordingly; the essay contrasts obedience to marriage duties with licentious or contemptuous conducts that undermine the contract.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not marry with hatred or contempt
rubrics_metrics.description: Those who engage in this contract with a design to carry themselves in it with hatred and contempt do an unjust and inconvenient thing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entering marriage while secretly hostile is morally wrong and practically destructive; sincerity of disposition toward the spouse is implied as a baseline requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid dissembling reverence (the 'serve thy husband but guard thyself' attitude)
rubrics_metrics.description: The popular rule among women — 'Serve thy husband as thy master, but guard thyself against him as from a traitor' — which counsels dissembled, inimical, and distrustful reverence, is injurious and hard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Feigning obedience while nursing hostility is an anti-pattern; genuine comportment is preferred to strategic deceit that creates conflict.

rubrics_metrics.name: Marriage and love are different ends — set distinct expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Marriage has utility, justice, honour, and constancy for its share; a flat but universal pleasure. Love founds itself wholly upon pleasure and has it more full, lively, and sharp; there must be in it sting and smart.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One should not expect marriage to provide the same passionate qualities as romantic love; recognizing the different purposes prevents misplaced demands and disappointments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledge and love marital duty even if not always performed
rubrics_metrics.description: If a man does not always perform his duty, he ought at least to love and acknowledge it; 'tis treachery to marry without espousing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inner assent to marital obligations is required; mere external compliance without endorsement amounts to betrayal of the contract.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be wary of double standards and male hypocrisy
rubrics_metrics.description: Men often excite women's desire and then blame them for it; we accuse women of vices while excusing the same in ourselves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criticizes unequal moral weighting of vices according to male interest; counsels self-awareness and fairness in judgments about sexual behaviour.

rubrics_metrics.name: Harsh legal decrees and extreme austerity often aggravate vice
rubrics_metrics.description: The austerity of our decrees renders the application of women to this vice more violent and vicious than its own condition needs, and engages it in consequences worse than their cause.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Overly severe laws or penalties can produce perverse effects; moderate, wise regulation is preferable to measures that exacerbate the problem.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize social and educational formation of sexual behaviour
rubrics_metrics.description: We train them up from their infancy to the traffic of love; their grace, dressing, knowledge, language, and whole instruction tend that way.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Behavior is shaped by upbringing and culture; blame or praise should account for social formation rather than assuming innate moral failing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modesty (when sincere) is the strongest allurement
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no allurement like modesty, if it be not rude and crabbed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Modest restraint, combined with goodwill, is more attractive than coarse or extreme styles of refusal; but affectation and excessive crabbedness spoil its effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rarity/scarcity increases the value of favours
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not consider how little it is that is given, but how few have it to give; the value of money alters according to the coinage and stamp of the place.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When judging the worth of favors or concessions, account for their rarity and the giver's disposition; small, rare concessions can be more telling than abundant ones.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chastity/virginity is an extraordinarily difficult and noble vow
rubrics_metrics.description: The vow of virginity of all others is the most noble, as being the hardest to keep.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affirms the exceptional moral difficulty and honour in maintaining chastity; this is praise meant to encourage steadfastness among women who keep it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jealousy and envy are foolish, destructive passions
rubrics_metrics.description: Jealousy, and envy, her sister, seem to me to be the most foolish of the whole troop.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Jealousy corrodes good qualities and produces disproportionate suffering; it alimentates itself from small causes and has few remedies — counsel against indulging it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing and opportunity are decisive in love
rubrics_metrics.description: What was the first thing to be considered in love matters, I should answer that it was how to take a fitting time; and so the second; and so the third—'tis a point that can do everything.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Successful attempts at seduction or courtship depend heavily on choosing the right moment; fortune and timing often matter more than raw will or desire.

rubrics_metrics.name: Men should display reverence, timidity, or servant-like humility in pursuit
rubrics_metrics.description: I would in this affair have a man a little play the child, the timorous, and the servant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A respectful, somewhat bashful approach preserves the allure and reverence that heightens desire; aggressive presumption tends to deface attraction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not mistake modesty-performance for truth; beware affected candour
rubrics_metrics.description: When 'tis spoken with an affected look, when their eyes give the lie to their tongue... 'tis good sport.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguishes sincere modesty from perfunctory or affected professions of coldness; affectation often signals the opposite and undermines credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exposure and visual familiarity can blunt desire
rubrics_metrics.description: Let the women of the kingdom of Pegu say what they will... yet, peradventure they lose more by it than they get, and one may venture to say, that an entire appetite is more sharp than one already half-glutted by the eyes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cultural practices that expose the body may reduce sexual appetite by familiarizing the sight; managing visual stimuli affects sexual appetite.

rubrics_metrics.name: There exist non-prostitute, non-intentional ways virginity may be lost
rubrics_metrics.description: There are ways by which they may lose their virginity without prostitution, and, which is more, without their knowledge... the midwife... has sometimes destroyed it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize accidental, medical, or malicious causes of loss of virginity; moral assessment should account for such possibilities rather than assuming voluntary fault.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public boasting of sexual favours is vulgar and harms reputations
rubrics_metrics.description: The ordinary discourse and common table-talk is nothing but boasts of favours received and the secret liberality of ladies... 'tis too abject, too much meanness of spirit, in men to suffer such ungrateful, indiscreet, and giddy-headed people so to persecute, forage, and rifle those tender and charming favours.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Boasting or public disclosure of private sexual favors is dishonourable and degrades both parties; discretion preserves honour and reputation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judge a person's constancy by conduct over time, not immediate slander
rubrics_metrics.description: Some whose reputation has for a great while suffered under slander, who have afterwards been restored to the world's universal approbation by their mere constancy without care or artifice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Constancy and sustained virtuous behavior can repair reputational damage; do not accept slander as definitive—time and steadiness are corrective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize the natural strength of female desire and the difficulty of restraining it
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no passion so hard to contend with as this, which we would have them only resist... we would have them at once sound, vigorous plump, high-fed, and chaste; that is to say, both hot and cold.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advises empathy and realism: female sexual appetite is powerful and culturally reinforced; unreasonable expectations of simultaneous vigor and chastity are hypocritical and unworkable.
